To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pion lattice structures may be formed during the hadronization of the quark-gluon plasma, (2) the pion lattice structure can be detected by analyzing the transverse momentum distributions of charged pions, and (3) the formation of the pion lattice is related to the suppression of fluctuations in net charge and banyon number after sudden traversal of a first-order QCD phase boundary in heavy-ion collisions

the observed correlation structure of like- and unlike-sign pions in high-energy pp collisions is a signature of a 3D pionic lattice formed during hadronisation, and that this lattice can be detected in the transverse plane of heavy ion collisions by measuring local transverse Hubbles.

(1) the pion lattice structure in HI transverse phase space is a direct consequence of the local Hubble flow; (2) the local Hubble-flow-induced correlation structure can be measured in the transverse plane; and (3) this structure is related to suppression of net-charge and baryon number fluctuations after sudden traversal of QCD phase transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel correlation structure in the transerve phase space of heavy ion collisions.
the structure of the hadronization phase of QCD.
the structure of the QCD vacuum and the nature of the QGP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lattice structure in transverse phase space is a signature of the QCD critical point, but that this signature is not conclusive.
the pion lattices are formed in the transverse plane and the rapidity direction is the direction of propagation of the pion lattice in the transverse space.
pion lattice structures are a natural consequence of the QGP phase and can be used to study the QGP phase in heavy-ion collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QCD phase transition in heavy-ion collisions may be detected in the transverse and longitudinal phase spaces by measuring the local transverse flow and the local rapidity flow.

a pion lattice structure in the transvers phase space of heavy ion collisions is a necessary and sufficient condition for suppression of net charge fluctuations and baryon number fluctuations in the final state of heavy ion collisions.
the lattice structure in transverse phase space may be the signature for the formation of the QGP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion lattice is an important ingredient of QGP hydrodynamics and may be used to test the hydrodynamic picture.
the QGP phase transition may be a {\em sudden traversal of the critical surface} rather than a continuous process.
the lattice structure of hadronic matter may be detected by measuring the transverse Hubble-flow of hadrons.
